## Tours through Baltra: choosing a Galápagos itinerary

[Baltra Island](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) lies off the northern coast of [Santa Cruz](/ecuador/place/santa-cruz-island/). It has the airport through which many travellers reach the Galápagos. But a mention of Baltra in an itinerary primarily indicates an **arrival or departure point**, not a full day of sightseeing on the island.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} that feature Baltra on the main route. The best way to choose is to look at where the group goes after the airport: a hotel on Santa Cruz, dive sites or a cruise vessel.

## What happens after arriving on Baltra Island?

For land-based programmes, the usual logistics involve travelling from the airport to the Itabaca Channel, crossing to Santa Cruz and continuing by transfer to [Puerto Ayora](/ecuador/place/puerto-ayora/). This sequence is included, for example, in ["Ecuador and the Galápagos: Discovering the Best Nature Reserves"](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/).

Cruises operate differently: an airport meet-and-greet may lead directly to boarding a yacht. Confirm the embarkation and disembarkation ports in advance. Not every cruise starts at Baltra, and the island may only appear in the description on the final day, when travellers return to the mainland.

Allow sufficient time on arrival day for airport procedures, baggage collection, ground transport and the channel crossing. The actual flight schedule determines how many additional stops are possible that day.

## Four ways to travel

| Tour | Main features |
|---|---|
| [4–5-day diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) | Santa Cruz and diving |
| [8-day VIP yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) | Several islands with accommodation aboard |
| [Ecuador over New Year, 11 days](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) | The Andes, cities and the Galápagos |
| [Active Ecuador, 17 days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) | Trekking and activities on the mainland, followed by the islands |

The [diving programme](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/) offers a 4-day option with 2 diving days and a 5-day option with 3 diving days; accommodation is provided at Hotel Fiesta. This tour should be compared by dive sites, eligibility requirements and the number of dives rather than duration alone.

The [eight-day yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) spends most of the journey at sea. Baltra is the point for returning to the airport, while the attractions are spread across several islands. This is a different kind of trip from staying in one hotel.

The [11-day New Year tour](/ecuador/tour/complete-ecuador-new-year/) visits Quito, Quilotoa, Baños and other mainland destinations before the archipelago. The [17-day active programme](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) adds longer treks and other activities. Compare how many days are actually spent in the Galápagos after the mainland portion.

## Which expenses and conditions need separate attention?

Tours vary in which flights, transfers, entrance fees, island excursions and accommodation are included. A transfer on Baltra cannot automatically be assumed to cover any other travel around the archipelago. For a cruise, cabin type and the vessel's route matter; for a land tour, look at accommodation, islands visited and daily excursions.

The [Galápagos Islands](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) have conservation regulations and special access arrangements for certain sites. We help coordinate the sequence of flights, inter-island transfers and excursions with the planned itinerary.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Baltra

### Do you need to cross from Baltra to Santa Cruz?

Yes, if your journey continues overland on Santa Cruz: the islands are separated by the Itabaca Channel. Cruise transfers and boarding arrangements may differ, so read the itinerary for that specific day.

### Can Baltra count as a separate excursion on a tour?

No. In many tours it is only the point of arrival or departure. A dedicated excursion on the island must be described with its own activities.

### Which tour is best for diving, and which for visiting several islands?

For diving, there is a [specialised 4–5-day tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/). For a cruise between islands, consider the [eight-day yacht itinerary](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/) if its actual stops match your interests.

### Do all journeys through Baltra also include mainland Ecuador?

No. There are standalone island programmes and longer journeys including Quito, the Andes and other regions. Browse the full [Ecuador tours catalogue](/ecuador/tour/) and check the number of days allocated to each stage.

## Baños, Ecuador: waterfalls, hot springs and mountain walks

Baños de Agua Santa is a town in Ecuador's Tungurahua Province, on the eastern slopes of the Andes. Tungurahua Volcano rises nearby, and the road towards the Amazon descends through the green Pastaza River valley. That setting defines Baños: in a single day, you can see several waterfalls, walk through a wooded gorge and relax in thermal pools in the evening.

For travellers, it is a convenient stop between the highlands and the humid eastern regions of [Ecuador](/ecuador/). Visitors come for both scenery and sport: canyoning, cycling, rafting and trips to viewpoints are offered here. Choose particular activities according to their physical demands and itinerary conditions, not merely the broad label "adventure activities".

## The Waterfall Route: what to see

The Ruta de las Cascadas runs from Baños along the Pastaza Valley. It connects several waterfalls, each with its own access conditions and views from the lookout points.

- [Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) is one of the best-known waterfalls on the route out of Baños and fits naturally into a series of stops along the valley.
- [Bride's Veil, or Manto de la Novia](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/), is known for slender streams of water falling down a green slope. Sightseeing programmes sometimes include a cable crossing to view the gorge.
- [Devil's Cauldron, or Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/), draws visitors with its powerful flow and walkways near the water.

The name "Waterfall Route" does not mean there is one fixed itinerary that visits every stop. Trail and viewpoint access, transport and stopping points vary by programme. The surroundings can be very wet, making walkways and steps slippery.

For a full sightseeing day, we offer a [waterfall route and the "End of the World" swing excursion](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/). Its description includes Agoyán, Bride's Veil, Devil's Cauldron, the Pastaza Valley, Casa del Árbol and onward travel to Riobamba. This programme is considerably busier than a relaxed drive to a single lookout.

## Hot springs: what to know before visiting

The town's name is associated with water: Baños is known for thermal pools fed by geothermal springs around Tungurahua. Popular complexes include La Virgen and El Salado. These are places to bathe and relax after travelling along mountain roads.

Water temperatures, opening hours and availability of individual pools differ. If hot springs are a priority, include them separately in the itinerary and confirm the exact complex. Merely mentioning Baños in a tour **does not establish that bathing and entrance tickets are included**. Nor should promotional claims of "healing properties" be treated as personal medical advice.

Hot water does not suit everyone equally; people with cardiovascular conditions or other restrictions should discuss a safe bathing routine with a doctor in advance.

## Swings over the valley and exploring the town

Another recognisable attraction is [Casa del Árbol](/ecuador/place/casa-del-arbol/), a swing viewpoint often called the "End of the World". Visitors come for views of the mountains and gorges. Visibility depends on clouds, while use of the swings must follow the site's rules and current weather conditions.

In central Baños, make time for the Basilica of the Virgin of the Holy Water. Its stone facade and local religious traditions reveal another side of the town beyond canyons and hot springs. This walk fits well into a less demanding part of the day.

Tungurahua Volcano can be seen from the surrounding area in suitable weather, but its proximity makes it important to heed official updates on volcanic conditions. Saying "the volcano is constantly erupting" would be inaccurate: activity levels vary, and travel decisions should be based on current monitoring.

## Baños for relaxed and active travel

| Style | What to focus on |
|---|---|
| Relaxed day | Town centre, hot springs, one viewpoint |
| Nature excursion | Agoyán, Bride's Veil, Devil's Cauldron |
| Active day | Canyoning or rafting with an instructor |
| Family outing | Short walks adjusted for the weather |

For water sports and canyon activities, check technical difficulty, health requirements and the equipment provided. After heavy rain, water levels and route conditions change. A family visit to viewpoints and a roped descent down a waterfall are very different products, even if both start in Baños.

The [nine-day "Active Ecuador" tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) devotes a day in Baños to canyoning with three descents and a visit to Pailón del Diablo. The [14-day "Ecuador and the Galápagos: Nature Reserves" itinerary](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-nature-discovery/) combines the waterfalls of Baños with the Andes, cloud forest and the Galápagos archipelago. The tours differ in exertion and geography; compare their actual days and included activities.

## How much time to allow and when to go

Part of a day can be enough for a short stop if your aim is the town centre and a thermal complex. Allow a full day for the Waterfall Route with several stops. Active sports need their own time slot and sometimes an extra overnight stay, especially if the journey continues towards the Amazon.

Baños has humid, changeable weather: light rain can fall in any month. Bring non-slip footwear, rain protection and dry spare clothes. It may feel warmer here than in Ecuador's highlands, but wind at viewpoints and spray near waterfalls can make you cold quickly.

## Frequently asked questions about Baños

### What should you see in Baños in one day?

If you prefer nature, choose part of the Waterfall Route, such as [Agoyán](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/) and [Devil's Cauldron](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/). For a more relaxed visit, leave time for the thermal pools and town centre.

### Can you combine hot springs and waterfalls?

Yes, provided you allow time for transfers and check the specific thermal complex's opening hours. Hot spring admission is not automatically included in every tour that stops in Baños.

### Is Baños suitable if you do not want extreme sports?

Yes. You can walk around the centre, enjoy the mountains and waterfalls from accessible viewpoints and relax in thermal pools. Canyoning and rafting are selected separately according to experience and fitness.

### Where can I find confirmed excursion itineraries?

Start with the [Ada Tours Waterfall Route excursion](/ecuador/banos/banos-waterfalls-and-swing/) or compare [Ecuador tours](/ecuador/tour/) that include Baños as a scheduled stop.

## Tours through Baños: waterfalls or an active adventure

[Baños](/ecuador/place/banos/) lies on the eastern slope of the Andes near Tungurahua Volcano. The town is known for hot springs and waterfalls, but visits can take very different forms. Some programmes offer sightseeing, while others involve waterfall descents, rafting and onward travel along an extensive mountain itinerary.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with Baños on the main route. The specific days and activities are more important to your choice than the tour title alone.

## The Waterfall Route: what is included

Around Baños are [Agoyán Waterfall](/ecuador/place/agoyan-waterfall/), [Bride's Veil](/ecuador/place/manto-de-la-novia-waterfall/) and [Pailón del Diablo](/ecuador/place/pailon-del-diablo-waterfall/). Several programmes visit these sites during a journey through the Pastaza Valley. However, the order of stops and walking portions vary; seeing Baños on a destination list does not confirm a visit to every waterfall.

On the [11-day "Best of Ecuador" tour](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/), the town forms part of an extensive route through Quito, Quilotoa, Riobamba, Chimborazo, Cuenca and the Galápagos. It suits travellers for whom Baños is one important nature experience within the broader aim of discovering different parts of the country.

The [nine-day "Active Ecuador" itinerary](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) takes a different approach: a canyoning day in the Río Blanco area with 3 waterfall descents, followed by a visit to Pailón del Diablo. The programme then continues with rafting on the Jatun Yacu River. Its physical demands should not be equated with an ordinary coach excursion.

## How the Ada Tours itineraries differ

| Programme | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Active Ecuador, 9 days](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) | Canyoning and rafting |
| [Active Ecuador and Trekking](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador-trekking/) | Mountain ascents before Baños |
| [Best of Ecuador, 11 days](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) | Cities, volcanoes and the Galápagos |
| [Activity Tour, 17 days](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) | Longer active portion and the islands |

The ["Active Ecuador and Trekking" programme](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador-trekking/) passes high-altitude landmarks including Rucu Pichincha, Pasochoa, Rumiñahui, the Ilinizas, Quilotoa and Chimborazo. Baños comes after the mountain section. If long climbs and changes in altitude are not what you want, consider a journey with sightseeing stops instead.

The [17-day tour with the Galápagos](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) includes trekking, rafting on the Quijos River, Baños and subsequent island excursions. It requires more time and readiness for changes in activities, elevation and climate.

## Planning a stop in Baños

Check how many nights are allocated to the town and how arrival day is spent. A quick transfer with waterfall stops is different from a full canyoning day. In some journeys, Baños marks the transition from the highlands to the humid foothills of the Amazon.

On Andean itineraries, it can be combined with [Quilotoa Lake](/ecuador/place/quilotoa-lake/) and the thermal area of [Papallacta](/ecuador/place/papallacta/), but Papallacta is a separate destination. Hot springs in both places do not mean bathing is automatically included in every tour's price.

Before choosing a sports programme, check the required exertion, safety briefing and equipment specified for that day. After rainfall, waterfall trails can be slippery; even an ordinary sightseeing walk may involve steps and wet surfaces. Mountain treks create cumulative fatigue over several days, so assess the entire route rather than one stage alone.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through Baños

### Which tour includes canyoning?

The [nine-day "Active Ecuador" tour](/ecuador/tour/active-ecuador/) includes 3 waterfall descents around Río Blanco. Read that day's description and participant requirements carefully.

### Can you visit the waterfalls without canyoning?

Yes. Sightseeing visits to waterfalls feature in other types of programmes. Confirm the particular stops and whether steps or wet trails must be negotiated.

### Are there tours that include Baños and the Galápagos?

Yes. For example, [11-day "Best of Ecuador"](/ecuador/tour/best-of-ecuador-guaranteed-departures/) and the [17-day active programme](/ecuador/tour/ecuador-galapagos-adventure-17-days/) combine the mainland with the archipelago.

### Are thermal pool visits included?

Not in every programme. Baños's reputation as a thermal resort does not mean admission is automatically provided. Check the daily itinerary and list of paid-for visits.

## Mirador de la Baronesa: Floreana's historic lookout

**Mirador de la Baronesa (Baroness Lookout)** is a viewpoint on [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the [Galápagos archipelago](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/). From the elevated spot, you can see the bay, coastal vegetation and volcanic landscape. The island's history also draws visitors: the lookout is associated with a woman known as the "Baroness" and mysterious events involving Floreana's settlers in the early twentieth century.

This stop appeals to people who want to combine **natural scenery with the history of settlement on remote islands**. The walk usually does not take a whole day, but arrangements depend on the overall sea itinerary and the visiting regulations at that particular part of the island.

## Where is the lookout?

The Mirador is on Floreana's northern coast. Rocky stretches, the bay and mangrove vegetation line the shoreline, while the trail leads to higher viewpoints. In clear weather, the contrast between the water, dark volcanic shores and dry scrub is particularly striking.

Visitors normally reach the viewpoint by a short trail from the landing site. The final part may involve a steeper climb with steps. Sturdy shoes and care on uneven ground therefore matter even on a brief excursion; accessibility must be assessed against the actual conditions.

The lookout is a distinct location, although it is often mentioned on the same itinerary as [Post Office Bay](/ecuador/place/post-office-bay/). One stop centres on a panorama and the Baroness's story; the other on a maritime postal tradition. They should not be treated as a single attraction.

## Who was the Baroness of Floreana?

In the early 1930s, several small groups of European settlers lived on Floreana. Among them was **Eloise Wagner de Bousquet**, who called herself a baroness. Her unusual lifestyle and relations among the island residents became part of Floreana's widely known history.

In 1934, the baroness and one of her companions disappeared. The circumstances remain disputed, with no confirmed final explanation in reliable historical accounts. Several other tragic events also occurred on the island that year. This is why the settlers' story is sometimes called the "Floreana mystery".

During a visit, it is best to understand this account as **history with documented facts and unresolved questions**. Tourist legends about the reasons for the disappearance should not be presented as proven events.

## What can you see from Mirador de la Baronesa?

From above, you can appreciate the shape of the shoreline and the arrangement of the small bays. Mangroves create green patches near the water, while the island's dry vegetation contrasts with the forests on wetter, higher parts of other islands. This helps reveal the varied natural environments of the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/).

The view is especially interesting after approaching the coast by boat. From the water, you see cliffs and mangroves; from the lookout, you can take in the broader outline of the coast. However, access to particular mangrove areas and the possibility of walking by the shore depend on the actual landing plan. A visit to the lookout does not guarantee an independent walk along the beach.

Wildlife should be observed from the permitted distance. Floreana's coast is part of the national park environment, so noise, feeding animals and attempting to approach them are inappropriate.

## Including the stop in a Floreana itinerary

A visit to the lookout usually forms part of an organised sea journey rather than public urban transport. Confirm whether a landing is scheduled, where it will take place and the order of stops.

If the programme also features [Post Office Bay](/ecuador/place/post-office-bay/), the two sites can be viewed as different chapters of the island's history. The bay evokes sailors' old postal tradition; the Mirador offers coastal views and stories of twentieth-century events.

Other marine nature destinations near Floreana include [Enderby Islet](/ecuador/place/enderby-islet/) and [Champion Islet](/ecuador/place/champion-islet/). Visiting the lookout and diving near these islets are different excursion products. Combining them depends on the permitted itinerary, weather and transport.

## When to visit and how to prepare

Floreana lies within the Galápagos' oceanic climate. Wind, sunshine, sea mist and water conditions can change, so closed shoes with non-slip soles, sun protection and light waterproof clothing are useful for a short landing.

Follow the route indicated by your local guide. The islands' protected status means that some areas are accessible only through approved visitor arrangements. Do not choose your own way to the lookout using a random online map without accounting for these restrictions.

The Mirador is most suitable for travellers interested in **island history, coastal landscapes and a relaxed scenic walk**. Explore other destinations in the [Ecuador places catalogue](/ecuador/place/) or the [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/) section.

## Frequently asked questions about Baroness Lookout

### Where is Mirador de la Baronesa located?

On the northern coast of [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in Ecuador's Galápagos archipelago, near a scenic shoreline and mangrove-lined bay.

### How is the Baroness's story connected to the lookout?

The name recalls Eloise Wagner de Bousquet, who lived on Floreana in the 1930s. Her disappearance in 1934 remains a historical mystery that has inspired many theories.

### Can you visit the Mirador independently?

Access depends on current national park regulations and the specific sea itinerary. In practice, landings of this kind should be arranged with an operator familiar with permitted visitor sites.

### Are Mirador de la Baronesa and Post Office Bay the same place?

No. They are two different [Floreana](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) attractions that may appear on the same itinerary but tell different stories.

## A tour through Mirador de la Baronesa on Floreana

[Mirador de la Baronesa](/ecuador/place/baroness-lookout/) lies on the northern coast of [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/) in the Galápagos archipelago. From a modest height, there are views across a mangrove-lined bay, turquoise water and volcanic shores. The place is associated with a woman who called herself a baroness and mysteriously disappeared on the island in the 1930s.

This is a stop within an island journey, not a standalone multi-day product. Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with the lookout on the main itinerary.

## What the Ada Tours cruise includes

On the [eight-day Galápagos VIP yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), Mirador de la Baronesa is included on **day 2**. The vessel reaches Floreana, where travellers discover its coastal landscapes and the history of settlement in the archipelago.

The same day's itinerary describes Punta Cormorant, with its coastal birds, and possible kayaking or snorkelling around Devil's Crown. The group then visits Baroness Lookout, where the guide recounts the baroness's disappearance and the island's legends.

These are separate parts of the day's itinerary. A visit to a natural lagoon, an activity on the water and a walk to a viewpoint have different characteristics. You can verify the precise combination of activities and what is included in the [cruise description](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/).

The cruise lasts 8 days and 7 nights, with accommodation on the yacht. After visits to several islands, the programme concludes with a transfer to [Baltra](/ecuador/place/baltra-island/) airport. Floreana is thus part of a continuous sea itinerary, not a day trip from a mainland hotel.

## Why choose a stop at Baroness Lookout?

Many people visit the [Galápagos](/ecuador/place/galapagos-islands/) for birds, marine animals and volcanic shores. Baroness Lookout adds a historical dimension: early settlers lived in isolation, and some events on Floreana remain the subject of competing accounts and legends.

A short walk to the panorama offers a view over the island's northern coast. The viewpoint appeals to those who value geography and history as much as wildlife watching. It is not a long trek: the main experience is the view of the bay and the guide's story.

Trails may have steps and uneven ground. Visits to protected sites depend on the permitted route, conservation rules and landing conditions; unrestricted independent access cannot be promised at any time.

## How to choose a cruise with this stop

Not all archipelago journeys visit Floreana, and mentioning Floreana alone does not prove that Baroness Lookout is on the itinerary. When comparing cruises, check the named places on each day: Punta Cormorant, Devil's Crown and Mirador de la Baronesa are separate destinations with different visiting formats.

If your main interest is the viewpoint and Floreana's history, choose the [eight-day Ada Tours yacht itinerary](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), where it is explicitly named. If underwater diving is your priority, we also offer a separate [Galápagos diving tour](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-diving-4-5-days/); a stop at Baroness Lookout should not be assumed on that programme.

## Frequently asked questions about tours to Baroness Lookout

### Where is Mirador de la Baronesa?

On [Floreana Island](/ecuador/place/floreana-island/), not Baltra or Santa Cruz. It is one of the named visitor sites in the Galápagos archipelago.

### On which day of the Ada Tours cruise is the lookout visited?

It is listed on day 2 of the [eight-day yacht cruise](/ecuador/tour/galapagos-luxury-yacht-cruise-8-days/), during the Floreana visit. Check the confirmed departure's itinerary before travelling.

### Is this a difficult hike?

No. It is essentially a short walk to a lookout. However, there may be steps and uneven ground, while access itself depends on landing conditions and park rules.

### Is the lookout included in every Galápagos cruise?

No. Island programmes visit different sets of places. Look for an explicit mention of Mirador de la Baronesa rather than just "Galápagos" in a tour title.
